summary: Open steel tower with an L-4 cab on Cibola NF land beside Kirtland AFB, built for the Department of Defense; construction date unknown; registered 2022.

facts.design: appears to be a 30-foot K-brace open steel tower with an L-4 cab atop (Register's tentative description)
facts.status_note: Standing, but the Register rates the structure in poor condition

access.note: Register notes Kirtland AFB lies just west; tDAR lists Forest Service land withdrawn to Kirtland and DOE nearby. No visitor rule in the sources read

events.note: Section 110 cultural survey of 6,000 acres of Forest Service lands withdrawn to Kirtland AFB and DOE in the Manzanita Mountains, fieldwork June to November 2002; the report is indexed under the keyword Manzano Lookout Tower
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register as US 1652, NM 51 on July 7, 2022

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Register says the tower is administered by the US Department of Defense with the Cibola National Forest as cooperator, while the survey record describes the surrounding land as withdrawn from Forest Service control. Both are cited; the story says the land is partly withdrawn and does not say who controls the tower.

notes_for_editor: Construction date and original builder remain unknown; the Register says so and no source read dates the tower. The tDAR keyword links the tower to a 2002-2003 survey of Forest Service land withdrawn to Kirtland AFB and DOE in the Manzanita Mountains, but the record gives no build or use date for the tower. The GlobalSecurity Manzano Base page (read, not used) describes a DoD weapons site whose construction began in 1947; no source read ties the lookout to that work, so it is not in the story. The Westlookouts Manzano page gives only a header ('Department of Defense'). Access is recorded as restricted on land-status grounds; no visitor rule was found. Brief's agency entry matches the Register.
